public_rationale: OpenAI's October 16, 2019 report describes sensor-equipped cubes used for most experiments and identifies interaction with arbitrary objects as a long-term goal [e1]. This supports the central claim that the demonstration did not establish dependable open-ended manipulation [e1]. The hardware description needs qualification: the report also evaluated vision-only sensing with modified center stickers and no other cube modifications [e2]. OpenAI's October 15, 2019 announcement separately reported handling unfamiliar disturbances during the cube task; this supports robustness within that task, not dependable performance across substantially different objects and tasks [e3].
limitations: The selected documentation does not establish the precise claim that one demonstrated cube contained both sensors and LEDs.
Embedded cube sensors were not required in every reported variant [e2].
The reported research goals and task-specific results do not establish that future open-ended generalization was impossible [e1, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's 2019 Rubik's cube robot result, achieved on a sensor-instrumented cube in controlled lab conditions, did not guarantee generalization to the open-ended real world.

statement.excerpt: getting their algorithm to work for one object (which, cheesily, turned out to be a special Cube instrumented with sensors and LEDS, unlike a Rubik’s cube you’d buy in a store) in carefully controlled lab circumstances hardly guaranteed that the solution would work more broadly in the complex open-ended real world.

criteria.contradiction_condition: The reported work establishes dependable open-ended task generalization. Evidence that all reported results used ordinary unmodified cubes would also contradict the stated instrumental setup.

evidence.explanation: The report also evaluates vision-only sensing using a cube whose center stickers were altered. This materially qualifies any implication that all results depended on embedded cube sensors; it does not establish open-ended task generalization.

OpenAI reported real transfer and robustness to unfamiliar disturbances. Those results qualify the controlled-laboratory characterization but remain narrower than dependable performance across open-ended objects and tasks.
